revision: not recorded here — a manifest cannot name the commit that contains it, for the same reason it cannot contain its own hash. The release identity is version + revision + digest: two are in-tree, and the consuming project records the revision in its own pin and verifies with `pack_pin.py <root> --version <v> --sha <full-40-char-rev> --digest <d> --state <state>`. See docs/RP2.2-GATE.md.
digest_note: release-local framing. Verify a release with the tools/pack_pin.py that ships inside it; a manifest naming an algorithm the verifier does not implement fails as a version mismatch, not as tampering.
supersedes: 2.4.0 — not replaced; runs pinned to it stay pinned to it, and it remains byte-identical at 9d906ce6 with digest 7bc0a811. PATCH, derived rather than assumed: every change is enforcement of an already-promised guarantee, no tool, policy or capability is new, no contract key or CLI input is added or removed, and no public name is removed. `DesignRecord.problems` gains one keyword argument defaulting to 2.4.0's behaviour and `backend_contract` exports one function two existing callers now share. Cases that previously passed and now refuse are the repair: each is one where the report made a claim it could not support.
baseline_revision: 9d906ce64bd69cb1a29594a7110829da7df5d996 — the 2.4.0 release commit, and the revision this release's CHANGELOG entry states its delta FROM. Recorded so the delta is checkable rather than described: `tools/release_delta.py` reads it and reports any file this range added, or decision it recorded, that the version's own entry does not name.
version_semantics: PATCH: backward-compatible fixes, metadata/docs corrections, enforcement of already-promised guarantees. MINOR: new backward-compatible policy/tool/capability. MAJOR: incompatible authority, contract or migration change. VERSION is the single machine-readable authority (DECISIONS.md D11).
pin_instruction: a project records ROOT PATH and version and full 40-character sha and tree digest and state in PROJECT.yaml pack.*, and verifies them rather than copying them. All four identity fields are required: `root_path` says WHICH DIRECTORY, the other three say WHAT is in it, and a pin without the root is UNVERIFIABLE_LEGACY_PIN (tools/pack_migration.py) because the release it names cannot be identified. Adoption happens only at a capability boundary. A frozen release never mutates during a project run; verification failing mid-project is a stop, not a pin to refresh.
concurrent_use: several projects may pin this same release at once, or different qualified releases, provided each version resolves to a distinct immutable root. Operational state and Evolution Candidate inboxes are project-local and never written into this repository (DECISIONS.md D13).

external_installed_skills.authority: ADAPTERS, NOT AUTHORITY. Outside this release envelope, covered by no tree_digest_sha256, and changeable without a pin noticing. Where an adapter and this pinned pack disagree, the pinned pack wins. From 2.2.0 an adapter a project dispatches through is DECLARED AND VERIFIED under the project's own adapters contract (tools/adapter_pin.py, PROJECT.yaml `adapters:`) — this list is an observation of what was installed here, never a substitute for that declaration (DECISIONS.md D12, D14).

known_limitations: THE STATE IS IN_PROGRESS AND NO PROJECT MAY PIN THIS RELEASE. It is a candidate that closes six defects an independent full behavioural audit reproduced in frozen 2.4.0. The transition to QUALIFIED_AND_FROZEN is policy/hitl-matrix.md row 2, it is the founder's, it has not been taken, and nothing here infers it. The procedure is at the end of docs/RP2.4.1-GATE.md. 2.4.0 remains frozen, byte-identical and adoptable; this release does not move it, and no push, tag, remote or consumer migration is authorised or has happened.

THE DESIGN GATE READS PROVENANCE FROM THE REPOSITORY THE CONTRACT DECLARES, so a project whose design record lives OUTSIDE that repository gets a stated refusal rather than an established answer when it supplies --mutation-begins-at. That is failure mode 3 of the frozen repair design, taken deliberately: a design whose history cannot be read has not been shown to precede anything, and fail-closed with a named reason is the honest answer. Without --mutation-begins-at the binding is unchanged and still the documented weak path. Neither is widened here. A project wanting the strongest binding keeps its design record in the repository whose history binds it, which is what this release itself does.

THE MANIFEST COMPARISON ESTABLISHES PROVENANCE, NOT TRUTH. R5 compares this file with the one committed at the pinned revision, which closes the gap between what a reader verified and what a reader read. It does NOT establish that the claims here are true: no mechanism in this pack can count a release's tests or audit its own limitations, and a check whose message outran its reason is the defect pack_pin exists to refuse. The test population is checked against real collection by tools/tests/test_release_integrity.py, which is the component that does the work.

THE UNTRACKED ENUMERATION NOW MEASURES AGAINST THE RELEASE'S OWN .gitignore FILES and no longer honours core.excludesFile or .git/info/exclude. A consumer who deliberately relied on a global ignore rule to keep a local scratch file out of this report will now see that file reported. That is the intended direction — the release cannot see, ship or vouch for the operator's rules — and it is stated because it is the one behaviour change a consumer may notice without having done anything wrong.

THIS RELEASE'S OWN REPAIRS WERE NOT INDEPENDENTLY DESIGN-FALSIFIED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION THE WAY 2.4.0's WERE. The R1/R2 design record was frozen and committed before any implementation commit, and its provenance is checkable by the mechanism it describes, but it was read by one coordinator rather than sent to two independent readings first. The bounded reason is scope: this is a blocker-repair release against reproductions that already existed, not a new capability. The independent reading it did get is a repair-delta reading after the fact, recorded in the release packet.

A RENAMED RELEASE PREFIX SILENTLY DISABLED A PUBLIC-SAFETY ORACLE, AND AN INDEPENDENT READER FOUND IT. test_every_release_record_that_summarises_the_adjudication_carries_its_occurrence resolved the adjudication from the gate-record PREFIX; this release moved the prefix to RP2.4.1 and did not re-ship an adjudication under it, because the one it ships is still RP2.4's and the manifest still names it. The guard then skipped — and with the protected occurrence DELETED from known_limitations it still skipped, reproduced by execution. Its own comment already warned that a document edit must not switch it off; a FILENAME edit did. Repaired by resolving the record from the manifest's declaration, which is what this file's own _release_doc_prefix docstring argues for, and by failing rather than skipping when a declaration resolves to nothing. It also now reads every record the manifest declares rather than one prefix glob, and the first thing it did after being repaired was catch a real omission in this release's own gate record.

AN INDEPENDENT READING OF THIS RELEASE'S OWN REPAIRS RETURNED THREE BLOCKERS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS IN THE REPAIRS. The normalisation repair left a THIRD path: `qualification.identity_from_configuration` reads `surface` and `pool_id` for itself and carried its own inline copy of the rule, so `surface=un_known` completed an identity and graded `confirmed` — the exact defect the repair was for, one dimension along. The untracked-material repair used `--exclude-per-directory=.gitignore`, which reads the ignore files PRESENT in the working tree rather than the ones the release tracks, so an untracked `unreviewed/.gitignore` containing `*` hid itself and an unreviewed module while the pin verified; the comment claiming it read only tracked rules was false. The provenance repair was unreachable from an ordinary command line, because `problems()` returned before checking when no repository was given and the CLI defaulted one to None, so `--mutation-begins-at` alone still reported DESIGN FROZEN. Each was reproduced by the coordinator before repair, and each repair carries a subject mutant that dies.

REIMPLEMENTING GITIGNORE WAS A MISTAKE, AND A SECOND INDEPENDENT READING PROVED IT AGAINST REAL GIT. The repair for untracked ignore files read the tracked rules and matched them in Python. It was wrong in BOTH directions: a leading `/` was stripped, so an anchored root rule silently matched at every depth and HID material; a nested rule lost its bare-name recursion, so genuinely ignored files became findings; and leading, trailing and escaped whitespace, which Git treats as significant, was normalised away. The predecessor agreed with Git on every one of those cases. `pathmatch` is for patterns a PROJECT declares in its contract; a `.gitignore` is Git's file and Git is its only correct reader. The enumeration now supplies the release's rules to Git and lets Git match: per-directory discovery is pointed at a filename the tree does not contain, which removes every working-tree ignore file's authority including an unreviewed one, and the tracked root `.gitignore` is supplied explicitly. A differential against `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` over eight rule shapes now holds it.

THE SENTINEL FILENAME WAS THE SAME HOLE WITH A DIFFERENT NAME, AND A THIRD INDEPENDENT READING FOUND IT. `--exclude-per-directory=<name>` makes Git look for that name in EVERY directory it walks, not only the root; the guard checked only the root. So an untracked `anywhere/.gitignore-not-tracked-by-this-release` containing `*` hid itself and an unreviewed module while `pack pin verified` printed — the first repair's defect, reached through the filename chosen to close it, and the name is in the source for anyone to read. No chosen name is safe. The option is gone entirely: omitting it makes Git read no working-tree ignore file anywhere, tracked or not, and the release's own tracked `.gitignore` is supplied by absolute path with `--exclude-from`. An oracle now asks with the exact name the implementation once trusted.

A CHECKOUT COULD POINT THE VERIFIER AT A DIFFERENT DIRECTORY. `core.worktree` in the checkout's own configuration redirects what Git treats as the working tree, so the untracked-file enumeration described somewhere else entirely: an unreviewed module sat in the named release root and the pin printed `pack pin verified`. It is a PATH, not a program, so the hardened reader's program-valued neutralisation does not reach it. Found by an independent whole-candidate reading. The verifier now asks Git which directory it is answering about and refuses when that is not the root it was given — asked rather than neutralised, because a linked worktree sets this key legitimately and its toplevel IS its root, which is exactly the case a blanket neutralisation would have broken.

THREE FILTER CLOSURES WERE ASSERTED AND NEVER TRUE, AND THE WHOLE-CANDIDATE READING WATCHED ONE RUN. `filter.*.clean`, `filter.*.smudge` and `filter.*.process` sat in the closed table claiming to be reachable only through `--filters`, which this reader refuses as an argument. An ordinary `diff` converts the worktree through the clean filter regardless: a configured program executed twice while `program_valued_config` reported nothing to see. They are no longer listed, so they fall to the standing rule that a program-valued key with no named closure refuses. THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: a repository legitimately using clean or smudge filters — Git-LFS is the common one — is now refused by this reader. Fail-closed is the direction that cannot run somebody else's program; a project needing those filters governs that as its own decision. Neutralising them instead was rejected because filter names are arbitrary and an empty clean command makes Git fail rather than proceed.

A GOVERNED READ COULD ANSWER ABOUT A DIRECTORY NOBODY ASKED ABOUT, AND TWO BLOCKERS CAME FROM THAT ONE GAP. `core.worktree` redirected reads to a sibling, so a workspace gate reported no unclassified files while one sat in the project it was asked about; and a release archive unpacked into an ignored vendor directory let Git discover the ENCLOSING repository and return zero tracked paths, so the pin digested an empty tree and said confidently that a byte-identical release was not the pinned pack. `pack_pin` had grown a local check for the first of these and it did not help the other eleven callers. Git's own toplevel is now compared with the requested root inside `gitread`, once, for every caller, and the local copy is deleted. THE FROZEN DESIGN FOR THIS REPAIR WAS WRONG ABOUT ONE THING and the record says so rather than being reshaped to match the code: it also bound the resolved repository, on the premise that a linked worktree's git dir sits under its own root. It does not — it lives under the main repository — so that binding refused every linked worktree, which is the layout this pack develops in. Falsified by execution before anything was committed.

A REFUSAL'S REASON WAS DISCARDED ON THE WAY OUT OF THE PIN. `pack_pin` translates the guarded reader's exceptions so its callers' existing handling keeps working, and `CalledProcessError` renders as `returned non-zero exit status 1` while dropping its `stderr` — so a refusal that carefully named which directory Git was answering about reached the report as an exit code. Found while writing the oracle for the repair above. A refusal from the guarded reader now carries its own words, and lands in the UNESTABLISHED branch rather than escaping the verifier.

`--local` READ ONE FILE WHILE GIT APPLIED TWO. With `extensions.worktreeConfig`, Git also applies `config.worktree` — beside `config` in a main worktree, under `worktrees/<name>/` in a linked one — and `git config --local --list` never shows it. So a `filter.x.clean` declared there was invisible to the program-valued inspection while Git ran it on every worktree conversion: an independent reading configured one with two `git config` calls and watched it execute seven times through the guarded reader. The blind spot was in the standing rule the filter repair relied on, not in that repair. Both sources are inspected now. The extension key itself was always visible to `--local`, so this module had what it needed to ask the second question and asked only the first.

A SWALLOWED TIMEOUT CLEARED THE INSPECTION THE REPAIR HAD JUST WIDENED. The worktree-configuration read was wrapped in `except GitRefusal: pass`, reasoning that it errors when the extension is off. It does — and it also errors when it TIMES OUT, so a per-worktree configuration large enough to outlast a caller-supplied deadline returned an empty inspection while Git applied `filter.x.clean`, and the governed read proceeded. Reproduced against real Git at three deadlines by an independent reading, and again by the coordinator. The handler two branches below already refuses exactly this, in the same words, and was not mirrored. It is not caught at all now: that outer handler owns every way the read can fail.

A DEFENSIVE BRANCH ADDED BY THIS REPAIR WAS UNREACHABLE, AND MUTATION IS WHAT SHOWED IT. The first fix added its own `except` translating an unreadable worktree configuration into a finding. A subject mutant that deleted it left the test green, because Git validates `config.worktree` during the LOCAL read too — so a malformed or unreadable file fails before the worktree listing is attempted, and the existing handler answers. The branch is gone rather than kept as depth: two handlers for one question is the shape this release exists to remove, and a test passing through the other one is not evidence for this one.

A REFUSAL THAT WAS NOT AN INTEGRITY FINDING LOST THE SHAPE ITS CALLERS HANDLE. The translation preserving an integrity refusal's words tested which MODULE an exception came from, which caught `GitRefusal` too — so a checkout whose HEAD does not resolve, previously reported as `HEAD could not be read, so the revision is unverified`, raised out of `verify_pin` as an uncaught ValueError. Narrowed to the integrity refusal. Found by an independent reading of the repair that introduced it, and no test covered the path, which is how it shipped.

A PROJECT'S `repo_path` NAMES A REPOSITORY, NOT A SUBDIRECTORY OF ONE, AND THE ROOT BINDING NOW ENFORCES THAT. Binding every governed read to Git's own toplevel refuses a root that is a subdirectory of a larger checkout. Settled mechanically rather than assumed: `templates/PROJECT.yaml.template` documents the field as the working repository, and all four real projects on this machine point at repository toplevels. No supported or used layout is affected. A monorepo sub-project layout would be, and is not supported here; distinguishing it safely from a release archive nested in someone else's checkout — which presents the identical shape — would add a branch to a security boundary for a layout nothing declares.

TWO ORACLES WRITTEN FOR THIS REPAIR WERE GREEN AGAINST THEIR OWN DEFECT, AND MUTATION CAUGHT BOTH. One drove `rev-parse`, the single verb the root binding deliberately exempts, so it never reached the comparison it was named for; the other did not exist at all for the unresolvable-HEAD path, which is precisely how that regression shipped. Recorded rather than quietly corrected: a green test is not evidence until it has been shown to fail against the thing it claims to catch.

A RELEASE WAS REFUSED FOR THE WAY ITS PATH WAS SPELLED. `--exclude-from` was built from the root as the caller gave it and Git resolves it against the directory it is launched in, which is that same root — so a relative root with a path component became `root/root/.gitignore` and the enumeration failed on a byte-identical tree. Found by the same reading. The root is resolved to an absolute path first. Automated consumers were unaffected, because every one of them resolves the root before calling; this reached direct command-line and API callers.

A NESTED TRACKED `.gitignore` IS REFUSED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED. `--exclude-from` is root-relative, so a declaration inside a subdirectory cannot be given its per-directory meaning by this construction. The enumeration raises and the pin reports it as a finding. No release has tracked one, and the alternative — guessing the translation — is exactly what produced the defect above.

FIVE REPAIRED BRANCHES SHIPPED WITHOUT AN ORACLE IN THEIR OWN TEST FILE, AND THE SECOND READING LISTED THEM: the no-repository refusal, the CLI repository default, both binary provenance comparisons, and `pool_id`'s normalisation. Each now has one. The earlier mutation pass had killed two of these from a different test file, which is why they read as covered and were not.

BOTH `byte-for-byte` PROVENANCE COMPARISONS COMPARED DECODED TEXT, so a line-ending rewrite survived a check whose entire claim is that the content has not moved since its commit. Repaired by reading Git in binary on both paths and comparing against `read_bytes()`. Recorded because the wording was the thing that was wrong: the claim outran the comparison, which is the shape this pack refuses everywhere else.

THREE OF THIS RELEASE'S OWN NEW TESTS DID NOT DISCRIMINATE WHAT THEIR NAMES CLAIMED, AND AN INDEPENDENT READER PROVED IT BY MUTATION. A test called `both_identity_paths` exercised only the structured mapping — and the defect that survived was on the packed side. A provenance test failed at base-revision resolution before ever reaching the provenance check, so deleting that check left it green. A global-exclude test passes because the hardened Git boundary discards global configuration, not because of the enumeration it was cited for. Each is repaired or re-scoped to say what they establish, and the enumeration now has two oracles that do discriminate it. The whole earlier mutation pass is not invalidated by this — the enumeration mutant was killed by a sibling — but three citations were weaker than they read.

THE REPAIRED PUBLICATION GUARD STILL LOST COVERAGE SILENTLY FOR EVERY DECLARED RECORD EXCEPT THE ADJUDICATION: records were appended only when `is_file()` succeeded, so a manifest naming a record it does not ship quietly shrank the guard — the same shape as the prefix rename that disabled it, one field along. A declared record that is not there is now reported.

THIS SESSION'S COORDINATOR REPRODUCED THE PACK'S HEADLINE RECURRENCE CLASS BY BYPASSING THE MECHANISM THAT REFUSES IT. Thirteen undeclared shell waiters accumulated against one logical subject, each an `until pgrep ...; do sleep; done` loop whose own command line matched its own pattern, so every one reported the independent reader as RUNNING after that reader's turn had already failed. Falsified mechanically afterwards: progress.waiter_problems refuses every one of those commands as a class, including the exact self-matching shape, and two waits on one obligation derive RECOVERY_REQUIRED naming the doubled obligation. The pack enforces the property; the coordinator never used it, which is limitation 55 exactly — the liveness model governs DECLARED waits and a waiter written by hand and never recorded is outside it. Recorded as recurrence evidence against three existing classes rather than repaired, because a library cannot police shells its caller runs, and inventing an enforcement it cannot honestly provide would be worse than the disclosure.

`tests.passed` IS BOUND TO WHAT THE SUITE COLLECTS, NOT TO WHAT PASSES. test_the_recorded_test_count_is_the_count_the_suite_actually_collects compares the field against `--collect-only`. In this release's qualifying run collection and passes are equal, so the two figures do not differ here. They CAN differ: three tests skip on conditions of the host rather than of the release — a child reaped before it can be observed as a zombie, a denied nested sandbox, and a Git that cannot build SHA-256 repositories — and on such a host a run reports fewer passes than the recorded population without anything being wrong. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS ENTRY BLAMED THE ZOMBIE RACE FOR A SKIP THIS RELEASE ACTUALLY HAD, WHICH WAS WRONG: that skip was the publication-adjudication guard, disabled by the prefix rename and recorded above. The field name is older than the distinction and is not renamed here, because renaming a manifest key is consumer-visible and this is a bounded repair release.

A RELEASE-MACHINERY GUARD WAS REBOUND BY THE RELEASE IT WAS BLOCKING, WHICH IS A SHAPE WORTH NAMING. test_this_versions_changelog_entry_names_what_this_release_added required a range to add more than five files before it asserted anything; a bounded repair release adds two, so the guard made the release unshippable rather than checking it. The floor is now zero — vacuous only when a range adds nothing — and the completeness assertion is untouched. The reason it is a limitation rather than a repair: the change was made by the release that needed it, with no independent reader having asked for it first, and that is exactly the direction in which a guard gets weakened one justified step at a time. The CHANGELOG entry states it in full.

2.4.0's FREEZE IS HISTORY, NOT THIS RELEASE'S STATE. That release was moved to QUALIFIED_AND_FROZEN by the founder at HITL row 2 against a named candidate — version, revision, digest, pre-freeze state and test population all stated in the authorisation and all verified before the first freeze mutation — and it remains frozen, adoptable and byte-identical. THIS release is a candidate and no project may pin it; its own state is the first entry in this list. The sentence carried forward unchanged said `a project may pin this release` while `state` read IN_PROGRESS, which an independent reading caught: a manifest that contradicts its own state field about adoptability is the one thing a reader consults it for.

held prose 2931 lines against a ~2000 target (46.6% over, recorded not shaved). 1896 lines are in-release and that half is UNDER the target; the 1035 that put the total over are the two installed adapters, outside this envelope, covered by no digest and impossible for this pack to freeze — and counted anyway, because they are loaded every session. 2.3.0 was 2675 (33.8% over) on the same rule. Delete-before-adding was applied: the adapter's static table of model slugs was REMOVED rather than updated, because a table that is wrong about what exists is worse than no table. AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS PILOT-RUN PASS REWROTE THIS SENTENCE WITHOUT THE FIGURES and two guards failed within one suite run, which is the guards working: the figures here are read by test_the_release_packet_and_the_manifest_agree_on_the_prose_breach and by test_the_baseline_figure_this_release_quotes_is_the_baselines_own.

THE COORDINATOR REPRODUCED THE FAILURE CLASS THIS RELEASE SHIPS THE TOOL AGAINST, TWICE. Three hand-written background monitors matched their own command lines and could not terminate; after building the mechanism that refuses exactly that, the coordinator wrote a fourth one and had to retire it. The repair is structural (docs/RP2.4-D26-PROPOSED.md, proposed D27) and the bound is unchanged and unclaimable: a wait the coordinator never declares is invisible, because seeing it would mean policing the coordinator's own shell.

THREE MUTANTS TONIGHT WERE ILL-FORMED AND FIRST READ AS WEAK GUARDS. A matrix row edited in a cell the guard never parses; a CLI wrapper removed from a tool that already handled the inputs itself; a `-k` selector matching nothing. A mutant whose subject never sees it is not evidence — the same rule as fixtures, one level up — and the third is why tools/selector_evidence.py exists.

TWO DELTA READINGS FROM TWO PROVIDERS RETURNED NOT SOUND ON FOURTEEN FINDINGS, AND THE BLOCKER WAS THE DESIGN RECORD BEING RIGHT WHILE THE IMPLEMENTATION WAS NOT. The record said a command-line-matching waiter is refused AS A CLASS; the code was a five-literal denylist plus a fallback a shell COMMENT could satisfy, and six waiters walked past it — including one that observes nothing and can never end. Repaired by reconstruction: a waiter is governed only if `waiter_command` rebuilds it byte for byte. All fourteen findings were reproduced before repair and seventeen mutants die. THE REPAIRS ARE THEMSELVES UNAUDITED, which is the standing condition of any final repair.

ONE READING COULD NOT EXECUTE THE SUITE AND THE OTHER COULD, AND EVERYTHING THAT TURNED ON EXECUTION CAME FROM THE SECOND. It found the recorded test count irreproducible under an ordinary TMPDIR (a `-k` selector matching pytest's own generated directory name), and a shipped guarantee with NO ORACLE AT ALL — a mutant inverting the dashboard's derivation passed the entire suite. A reader that cannot run the subject reads a different thing, and the difference is stated rather than averaged into one verdict.

THE COORDINATOR SHIPPED THREE REPAIRS WITHOUT ORACLES AND A MUTATION PASS CAUGHT IT. Three of seventeen mutants survived their first run because the repair had been made and the test had not. `a repair with no oracle is a claim` is this pack's own rule, met by its own coordinator, in the release that states it.

THE BOUNDED READING OF THE REPAIRS FOUND TWO DEFECTS IN THE REPAIRS, AND ONE WAS THIS PACK'S OWN HEADLINE FAILURE. A repair gave `process_has_ended` a third answer for an unreadable process table, and the caller tested `if ended:` — so `None` read as `False` and a producer nobody could ask about reported as running. The other: a governed waiter was never bound to the wait it governs, so one watching an unrelated process was accepted. Both reproduced, both repaired, five mutants dead. A first draft of the first repair would have reversed an existing decision as a side effect — refusing a malformed pid at construction, where this module deliberately carries it and names a state — and was reverted.

THE COORDINATOR CHANGED THE SUBJECT UNDER A READING THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION: HEAD moved under the first release-authority round, HEAD moved under the first delta round, and an uncommitted file changed under the repair round. Each was detected and scoped correctly by the reader rather than by the coordinator. The rule is that a subject does not change under a reading and UNCOMMITTED IS NOT AN EXEMPTION; it is recorded here because three instances is a habit rather than a slip.

THE PER-CONFIGURATION QUALIFICATION TABLE IS SMALL, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE OF THIS EVIDENCE. No observation recorded before this release carries an observed model, an authentication class or an execution surface, so all of those are family-level prior and none is a track record. HOW MANY CARRY A COMPLETE IDENTITY IS NOT RESTATED HERE — it changed within one commit of being written and an independent reader caught the stale figure. Run `python3 tools/qualification.py`, which prints the count and both tables from the log. Every other configuration answers `unprobed` with a prior beside it. Nothing was fabricated to fill the table and nothing was deleted.

GPT-6 ASTRA IS PROVISIONAL WHERE IT HAS EVIDENCE AND UNPROBED EVERYWHERE ELSE, AND THE TASK CLASSES ARE NOT LISTED HERE — the list went stale within one commit and an independent reader caught it. `python3 tools/qualification.py` prints them with every keyed dimension, including the effort that makes two of them DIFFERENT configurations rather than one model at two task classes. It is NOT confirmed anywhere, and in particular it is `unprobed` at blind_closure_audit_cross_vendor where the family-keyed derivation returns `confirmed` on seven observations. One dispatch each against one alternative is a comparison and not a rate.

THE RELEASE-AUTHORITY READING RETURNED NOT READY ON FOUR BLOCKERS AND ONE WAS THE COORDINATOR'S OWN PROCESS. HEAD moved while the reading was in flight, so the auditor compared the earlier manifest against the later tree and correctly reported a digest mismatch that does not exist in either revision. The other three were real, reproduced by execution before repair, and each is closed by an oracle that fails against the pre-repair behaviour with the mutant killed: a provenance spelled `unobserved` reached `confirmed`; a declared probe filled the mandatory cross-provider leg AND THE ADOPTION REHEARSAL EXPECTED IT TO; and a whitespace producer established independence. THE REPAIRS ARE THEMSELVES UNAUDITED until a delta re-audit, which is the standing condition of any final repair.

THE RELEASE-AUTHORITY READING COULD NOT EXECUTE THE SUITE. Its read-only sandbox gives pytest no usable temporary directory, so it collected the suite, read it, and executed the candidate's sources in memory rather than running the tests or mutating files. Its coverage is reasoning and collection rather than execution, which is a real bound on what that round establishes and is stated rather than implied by the verdict.

THE TWO DESIGN READINGS OF THE QUALIFICATION DESIGN CAME FROM ONE PROVIDER THROUGH ONE CLIENT. They are independent of the coordinator and of each other's session, and they are NOT independent of each other's provider; tools/routing.py refuses exactly that pairing for a leg declared cross-provider. The final release-authority reading of this candidate IS cross-provider — see docs/RP2.4-GATE.md — so the gap is closed for the delta this release actually ships and stands as recorded for the design round.

AVAILABILITY WAS RE-ESTABLISHED ON THE CURRENT CLIENT BY DISPATCH, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THAT ESTABLISHES IT. Every earlier availability observation was recorded on client 0.149.0; the client moved to 0.153.3 because execution proved the older one could not run the model under evaluation. A live sweep dispatched every identifier discovery offers on the current client and every one started, with the model the surface reported matching the model requested. Figures in docs/RP2.4-GATE.md. Availability observed today is not availability tomorrow, and availability is never qualification.

A SURFACE THAT CANNOT REPORT THE EFFORT IT RAN AT CANNOT PRODUCE A COMPLETE IDENTITY. The keyed effort is the OBSERVED one, because this execution surface accepts an effort it will not run at. Where a surface reports the model and not the effort, the configuration stays incomplete and therefore unprobed. The remedy is in the adapter; this pack will not infer the value, because inferring it is the substitution the release exists to prevent.

THE CLIENT BUILD IS NOT IN THE QUALIFICATION KEY, AND THAT IS A CLAIM ABOUT THIS EVIDENCE BASE ONLY. Both independent readings were asked for an A/B pair where a build change altered what a configuration can do; neither could produce one from this log. The decisive falsifier is named in the design record, and tools/qualification.Invalidation is the governed response when it appears. It is not a claim that client versions are irrelevant — this session watched one refuse a model the next accepted, which is an AVAILABILITY difference and is keyed as one.

AN INVALIDATION THAT DROPS ADVERSE EVIDENCE CAPS THE IDENTITY AT `provisional` PERMANENTLY. It is what stops a declaration being used to delete a contradiction into a qualification, and it means a configuration whose adverse history was invalidated cannot reach `confirmed` again from evidence alone. Restoring it is a human decision, which is what declaring the invalidation was.

A DENYLIST OF UNOBSERVED PROVENANCE CANNOT CATCH A FABRICATED ONE. Completeness refuses the provenance markers an adapter actually writes when it did not observe an identity. An adapter that invents a method name passes. That is an explicit trust boundary — the independent reader that found the underlying defect said the same — and the alternative, an allowlist of admissible surfaces, is a vocabulary that ages exactly the way the model vocabulary this release replaced aged.

THE GENERATION PATTERN DOES NOT COVER A BARE CODENAME WITH NO VENDOR PREFIX. Deliberate: a bare codename is an ordinary word in some language, and this pack's own tiering rationale rests on a measured case where exactly that produced four findings and zero true positives. Such a name is caught where it appears with its prefix, and is otherwise a literal a project adds to its own vocabulary.

THE PACK'S OWN COMPLETE HISTORY IS ADJUDICATED RATHER THAN OWED, IN docs/RP2.4-PUBLICATION-ADJUDICATION.md. ONE OCCURRENCE NAMES A REAL MACHINE ACCOUNT and it is stated there: a historical blob reachable from the release branch carries a home directory that was redacted from the TREE at RP2.2, where a guard now holds it, and the redaction does not reach history. Remediable only by a rewrite, which is rows 2 and 4, and not taken. Every other occurrence at that tier is a home-relative form, a fixture path, a template placeholder or a synthetic identifier. A BOUNDED READING FOUND THAT CORRECTING THE ADJUDICATION HAD LEFT THIS ENTRY AND TWO OTHER RELEASE RECORDS REPEATING ITS ORIGINAL FALSE UNIVERSAL. At the STRICT tier the population is this pack's own governance vocabulary appearing in its own documentation — the case skills/core/public-safety.md describes, since this repository IS the denylist. Neither figure is restated here; the tool prints both. Whether this repository is ever published at all remains a founder decision needing a publication profile rather than a remediation list, and no first remote exists.
REVIEW_LOCAL contradicted on one observation; EXTRACT_LOCAL provisional on two. Carried unchanged from 2.3.0, and now readable as what it always was: family-level prior evidence.
relative yield between AUDIT_PRIMARY and AUDIT_CROSS is still unmeasured. The audits are not run as a comparison and a count is not a rate.

THE EVOLUTION WORKSPACE IS A LINKED WORKTREE, BECAUSE A LIVE PROJECT PINS THE PACK'S WORKING CHECKOUT BY ROOT PATH. That is the D18 layout defect the 2.2.0 manifest named as the finding most deserving a decision, and the LAYOUT is unchanged. What changed is that it is no longer prose: pack_pin.root_kind names a linked worktree, capability_open reports it beside a verified pin as a NOTE rather than a block, and a test executes the hazard — the pin fails loudly with four problems rather than quietly. Relocating that project's release root is the founder's decision and was explicitly not taken.

AN ADAPTER PIN VERIFIES THE EXECUTABLE A PROJECT DECLARES, AND NO REAL PROJECT DECLARES ONE YET. The mechanism is now exercised end to end by an adopting project in tools/tests/test_two_consumer_rehearsal.py — declared executable, version command and qualified version, with a drifted version refused rather than warned about and a required adapter edited after qualification stopping that project's capability while leaving the other project's alone. Every real contract on this machine still declares files only, so every real report still reads '0 executable(s)'. The declaration is the project's to make.

installed adapter skills and agents live outside this repository and are not covered by tree_digest_sha256; they are covered instead by a project's declared adapters contract, which is verified rather than frozen

PROSE CLAIMS ABOUT THIS RELEASE'S OWN HISTORY ARE CHECKED BY A READER, NOT BY A TEST, except where a guard binds one. 2.2.0 recorded this as the likeliest remaining defect in its candidate on four rounds' evidence, and this candidate inherits the condition unchanged.

THE ADAPTER PATH IS UNEXERCISED BY ANY REAL CONSUMER. One of the real projects on this machine declares adapters; the rest do not. It is now exercised by a rehearsal that declares one the way a real project would, which is a fixture standing in for an adopter rather than an adopter.

THE CAPACITY GATE HAS NEVER BEEN RUN AGAINST A LIVE PROVIDER READING. Every fixture supplies its own pool figures, and the one documented resource surface this pack can read (tools/resource_observation.py) reports UNKNOWN in the ordinary case by that surface's own definition. What is exercised is the arithmetic, the refusals and the conservative posture; what is not is whether a real reading arrives in the shape the gate expects.

THE DIAGNOSTIC PROJECTION SHIPS AGAINST THE EVIDENCE, ON A HUMAN DECISION. The reconciliation this release draws on refuses a dashboard in terms — a human wanting one is not evidence that Core should ship one — and the refusal is recorded rather than reversed. What answers its concrete objection is the ordering: coordinator state is derived rather than stored, so there is no stored value to go stale. It is a one-shot renderer with no port, no cache and no importer, and removing it is deleting one file.

A REAL PROJECT ON THIS MACHINE STILL CARRIES A PRE-2.1 CONTRACT and this release does not migrate it. The refusal now names the schema generation and the migration instead of reporting a type error, which is the repair; performing the migration is the project's, because the two private-term tiers differ in whether a term applies to blob content and choosing would change what gets scanned.

A CLOSE ATTESTATION DOES NOT VERIFY THAT A PROFILE RAN. The outcomes are supplied by the caller and the state is derived from the exit status the caller records; a caller that records a falsehood records a falsehood. What the mechanism makes impossible is SILENCE — a declared profile cannot be absent from the record. An earlier draft of the module's headline promised independent verification of what ran, which it does not provide; an independent auditor found the sentence and it is corrected rather than left standing.

A DESTROYED CITATION IS DETECTED BY LENGTH, NOT BY PROVENANCE. A forty-character object name this repository does not have is treated as a citation of something gone, and a shorter one as prose. That boundary is a judgement about how people write records, not a fact about Git: a forty-character token that never was a revision would be reported as destroyed. The alternative — treating every unrecognised hexadecimal word as a lost commit — produces a remediation list nobody can act on, which is the failure the adjacent publication work exists to prevent.

THE FAILURE-MODE CLOSURE MATRIX IS THE RELEASE'S OWN CLAIM AND IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY AUDITED AS A WHOLE. Each row cites a test or a rehearsal that can be run, and the auditors of round 1 exercised many of them individually, but no auditor has been asked to falsify the matrix as a document. Its five open residues are stated in it rather than in a summary.

A PATH-BASED WAIT CANNOT NAME A PRODUCER. An unrelated writer satisfies a PATH_EXISTS or EXIT_FILE wait, and no property of a bare filesystem path distinguishes who wrote it. The observation is strengthened as far as a filesystem permits — a regular file that does not predate its own wait — and OUTPUT_ROOT, whose owner marker is now checked on read as well as on write, is the kind that establishes a producer. A test pins both halves.

THE PROJECTION IS A READER AND HAS NEVER BEEN WATCHED DURING A REAL MULTI-HOUR RUN. It now renders as a page as well as as text, and both were falsified against twelve synthetic states, but nobody has yet watched either during a long run. Its fields are exercised against fixtures and against this session's own live record, where it correctly reported a stale record and an undeclared audit subject. Whether the information architecture is the right one for someone watching a Consumer-A run for six hours is not established, and cannot be until someone does.

THE PROGRAM-VALUED CONFIG LIST IS NOT COMPLETE AND CANNOT BE. It enumerates the shapes of Git config keys whose value is executed; Git may add another, and a key that matches no shape is not inspected. What the design buys is that an unrecognised key MATCHING a shape refuses rather than waiting to be found — the population of routes is open-ended and the population of shapes is smaller and slower-moving, not closed. It also costs two extra Git processes per repository per invocation, about 17 seconds on a 110-second suite.

ONE MECHANISM IS DEFERRED RATHER THAN COVERED: contract, classification and sandbox gaps, inherited from 2.2.0 with no discriminating oracle demonstrated in this release. Recurrence is bounded because the 2.2.0 contract checks ship unchanged and their tests still run, but that is inheritance rather than a demonstration made here, and the final evidence-closure check reclassified it rather than let it read as covered.

A FILESYSTEM CLONE DEFEATS THE CHUNK LINK-COUNT CHECK. `cp -c` on APFS puts one task's bytes in another's root with st_nlink == 1 on both, and nothing on disk distinguishes that from bytes the second task wrote. The ownership guarantee rests on the owner marker and the completion marker, both of which are checked; it does not rest on the bytes. Found by an independent reader in cycle 10, declared rather than closed, and now stated as a bounded guarantee with an oracle: what IS guaranteed is that two roots are never confused, which was executed and holds; what is not is that a root's bytes were computed by its owner. The error cannot cause unsafe acceptance.

THE CHUNK LINK-COUNT CHECK HAS A FALSE POSITIVE: a task that hard-links its own product into its own root classifies UNKNOWN. Wrong in the safe direction — UNKNOWN loses nothing, because `resume_plan` refuses to act on it — and recorded rather than narrowed.

`_bundle_contains` COMPARES BUNDLE TIPS ONLY, so a commit reachable inside a verified bundle but not named as a head reports UNREACHABLE. Safe direction: it blocks where it should anchor. Proving reachability inside a bundle means unbundling, and this release does not write.

THE ARTIFACT GUARDS COST ABOUT 60 SECONDS OF THE SUITE'S 171. `test_every_oracle_the_matrix_names_selects_at_least_one_test` spawns one pytest collection per matrix row, which spawn one pytest collection per matrix row and per recurrence class. Recorded because a check whose cost nobody measured is a check somebody eventually disables, and because the alternative — trusting that the selectors still match — is what it exists to replace.

A BUNDLE CANNOT ANCHOR ANYTHING IN THIS RELEASE. Establishing that a bundle carries a commit means indexing its pack, which is a write, so a verified bundle whose header names a cited commit yields ANCHOR_UNCONFIRMED and BLOCKS. That is strictly more conservative than 2.2.0's behaviour and it is a real cost: a project that anchors closures in bundles will find those closures blocked until a person adjudicates them. Revisit when a read-only way to enumerate a pack's objects is available, or when the write is authorised for a scratch index.

AN ORACLE SELECTING A TEST DOES NOT PROVE IT TESTS THE MECHANISM IT IS CITED FOR. The matrix guard establishes that every citation resolves to something that runs, which is strictly weaker than relevance. Relevance is a human judgement and no check here makes it; the citations were chosen by the coordinator and read by nobody else.

THE VISUAL IDENTITY IS CHOSEN AND IT IS ONE PERSON'S CHOICE. Monochrome is the default lens, the temperature is neutral-to-warm, no purple appears anywhere, and a FOUNDER preset and a FOUNDER CONTROL ROOM layout ship built in. Four other lenses ship beside it. What is established by test is that every lens holds contrast, perceptual tone separation and a readability floor that rises with the viewport, and that Matrix's large surfaces stay below a browser-computed luminance ceiling. What is NOT established is that these are the right choices for anybody else: they were made by looking at previews, and the settings panel exists because the next reader will disagree.

THE DASHBOARD HAS NEVER BEEN WATCHED DURING A REAL MULTI-HOUR RUN. Both renderers are falsified against twelve states, two themes and two viewports, and against this session's own live record. Whether the information architecture is right for somebody four hours into a Consumer-A run is not established and cannot be until someone is.

THE EVENT HISTORY IS DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE AND SAYS SO. Seven event classes ship because seven are what durable artifacts date; a capability opening, an audit being dispatched and a finding being recorded are not among them, because nothing writes their time down. One class, `deadline passed`, is arithmetic over durable fields and the clock rather than a recorded fact, and is marked `derived` and filterable for that reason. A durable event log is recorded as an Evolution Candidate, not shipped.

THE REMOTE SIDE OF REPOSITORY ACTIVITY IS AS OF SOMEBODY ELSE'S LAST FETCH. This release never contacts a network, so `REMOTE-REPRESENTED` is read from remote-tracking refs and is exactly as current as the last fetch performed outside it — which the view reports where the repository records it and declines to guess where it does not. A declared remote nobody has fetched reads REMOTE NEVER OBSERVED, which is not the same as a remote with nothing on it.

REPOSITORY ACTIVITY READS 366 DAYS BY DEFAULT, NOT A COMPLETE HISTORY. The window is a render-cost decision, `window_days=0` reads all of it, and the view names the window it read. A multi-year calendar is an Evolution Candidate.

NEITHER HISTORY IS EVIDENCE OF QUALITY, AND ONLY A TEST KEEPS IT THAT WAY. A commit count measures that commits happened. No productivity, velocity, developer or good-day figure is derived anywhere, and the guard that holds this is a vocabulary refusal over the rendered page rather than anything structural: a future contributor who wanted such a figure would have to delete a test to get it, which is the point.

THE DESIGN GATE CANNOT STOP A CALLER WHO DECLARES A MATERIAL CHANGE TRIVIAL. The change class is an input because Core cannot know which of a project's changes are material, and `TRIVIAL` resolves to NOT_REQUIRED. The declaration is recorded in the readiness report, so it is a visible claim an auditor can dispute rather than a silent omission — but it is detection by disclosure, not prevention, and D25 says so.

THE DESIGN GATE CHECKS THAT A DESIGN WAS MADE, NEVER THAT IT WAS GOOD. It reads a record and answers whether that record states alternatives, a rejection with a reason, failure modes, authority boundaries and frozen oracles. Whether the selected design is the right one is product meaning, which Core does not adjudicate. A well-formed record of a bad design verifies.

PERSISTENCE ACROSS A COLD BROWSER RESTART IS NOT VERIFIED ON THIS HOST. What IS verified this release, in a real browser: a lens, a view, a density and two disclosure levels survive a full page navigation and are read back from localStorage; and a CORRUPT stored value falls back to the default with no console error and a fully working page. Surviving a NEW BROWSER PROCESS is not verified, because headless Chrome hangs on this machine whenever --user-data-dir names a fresh profile and the alternative is a side effect on the operator's own browser. Storage outliving a process is the browser's guarantee, not this page's.

A SEMANTIC AND A NEUTRAL CAN STILL BE CLOSE AS TEXT. Separation is enforced across what the charts PAINT — ink, bad, warn, unknown, good — because those are areas a reader has to tell from the area beside them. As text, monochrome's warn sits near its dim, and every lens's restrained accent sits near its ink deliberately. Forcing those apart would contradict the brief the palettes were built to: UNKNOWN is steel in every lens, and the accent is meant to be quiet. Every state's text also carries a glyph, so colour is not the only channel — but colour alone does not distinguish them, and this says so.

THE LIVENESS MODEL GOVERNS DECLARED WAITS AND NOTHING ELSE. A wait recorded in the continuation record must name a deadline, and past it the state is RECOVERY_REQUIRED whatever the process is doing. A waiter a coordinator writes by hand and never records is outside that: the model cannot see it, and acquiring the power to see it would mean policing the coordinator's own shell. Measured in this release's own session — five undeclared waiters survived ninety-five minutes after their workers had exited. The pack ships `progress.waiter_command` so that a coordinator need not hand-write one; using it is discipline, not enforcement.

A PROJECT'S REPOSITORY WAS RESOLVED AGAINST THE PROCESS RATHER THAN THE PROJECT, AND IT TOOK RUNNING THE APPLICATION TO SEE IT. ProjectContract.repository() returned a relative `repo_path` verbatim — `"."` in every rehearsal fixture in this pack, and available to any project. AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS ENTRY SAID THE TEMPLATE SHOWS `repo_path: "."`; it does not, it says `# absolute path to the working repository`, and an independent reader checked — so the commit gate over a range, the outgoing scan, the workspace report and the publication gate all ran against whatever repository the invoking shell was in. The multiproject history view showed the coordinator's own commit count under two consumers' names. Repaired at the contract so every caller is correct at once, with five mutants dead. It is recorded here because no unit test could have found it: every rehearsal was single-project and ran from the project's own directory.

A TEST WHOSE EVERY ASSERTION SITS INSIDE A LOOP OVER A COMPUTED ITERABLE CAN PASS HAVING ASSERTED NOTHING, AND NO GUARD PREVENTS A NEW ONE. Thirty-six such tests exist. All thirty-six were traced under execution in this release and every assertion in thirty-five executed; the thirty-sixth executed two of four, which is branch coverage rather than vacuity. The population is measured clean and a shape guard would force cosmetic edits on thirty-six honest tests, so this is recorded as an Evolution Candidate rather than guarded.

MEASURING THE VACUITY OF THE SUITE PRODUCED A FALSE GREEN OF EXACTLY THE KIND IT WAS MEASURING. The trace harness reported all thirty-six loop-only tests as vacuous, from a pytest invocation that had matched no files and executed nothing — 'no tests ran in 0.00s' sitting above the result. The pack's own rule caught it (a run that executed nothing is not evidence) and the real answer is the opposite of the first one. Recorded because the tool that measures this failure class must itself prove it ran, and this one did not.

TWO DISPATCHES AT ONE CONFIGURATION REACH `confirmed` AT THAT TASK CLASS, INCLUDING TWO BOUNDED PROBES. That is backend_contract's grading rule, unchanged by D26 on purpose, and it is bounded by the task class: evidence at `model_usability_probe` qualifies nothing at `blind_release_authority_audit`, and HITL rows 12 and 16 keep their human for a critical-domain promotion. What it does mean is that a project choosing coarse task classes gets coarse evidence, which is a property of the project's classification rather than of the derivation.

AN INDEXED EDIT TO THIS LIST SILENTLY DESTROYED ONE OF ITS OWN ENTRIES, AND THE RELEASE SHIPPED THAT WAY UNTIL A READER FOUND THE SYMPTOM. A script rewrote entries by POSITION after having already removed two, so one assignment landed on a different limitation and overwrote it — the record of two local-model grades, restored here from the baseline by matching its text. An independent reader found the other symptom of the same edit: two entries about this pack's own history, contradicting each other, both shipping. Same class as the shell chain that landed a refused commit message: an operation whose target was COMPUTED rather than NAMED. Every edit to this list is now made by matching content.

THE REHEARSAL THAT PROVES BACKGROUND WORK IS NOT LEAKED, LEAKED BACKGROUND WORK. Its producers block until this test releases them, so a failure anywhere between starting them and releasing them left two processes waiting for a file that would never be written — and four of them sat for seventy-two minutes on this machine, in the release whose subject is phantom background work. A bounded independent reading injected the failure and found them; the release is now in a `finally`, and the same injection now leaves zero. Recorded because the mechanism was right and the thing exercising it was not, which is the harder half to see.

THREE OF THE FIVE DEFECTS A BOUNDED READING FOUND IN THE FIRST REPAIR ROUND WERE IN THE REPAIRS THEMSELVES. A rule that cleared an ambiguity when any supplied VALUE contained its words was walked through by supplying those words in an unrelated field; `os.path.normpath` collapsed `..` before the filesystem read a symlink, so a declaration naming one directory resolved to another; and repairing an adapter's FILE lookup made a combination newly reachable where the project's definition file was checked against another directory's executable. Each is recorded because the first repair of a class is where the second defect of that class lives, and this release has now met that three times.

THE GUARD WRITTEN TO STOP A DOCUMENTATION DEFECT RECURRING PASSED HAVING EXAMINED NOTHING. It normalised hyphens out of the text it searched and kept them in the strings it searched for, so no release record ever matched and the check was vacuous — in the suite that ships its own vacuity sweep, in a guard written during a round about false claims. Repaired, and the guard now asserts how many records it examined, because a check that matches nothing and a check that finds nothing produce the same result.

AN ORACLE THAT ENUMERATES THE FIELDS OF A RECORD LOSES A RACE IT CANNOT WIN. Two bounded readings in succession defeated the guarantee that a family prior ranks nothing, each by keying a rank on a field the fixtures left at zero — `contradicted`, then `synthetic_observations` — and each repair widened the parametrisation and was defeated by the next field. The oracle now hands the ranker a prior whose evidence RAISES on access, which no field-keyed change can survive. Recorded because the two repairs before it were each reasonable and each wrong, and the lesson is about the shape of the oracle rather than about the field.

THE GUARD ON THE PUBLIC-SAFETY SUMMARIES CATCHES AN OMISSION, NOT A LIE, AND FOUR ROUNDS ESTABLISHED THAT THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT CLOSEABLE. Three successive versions were defeated by an independent reader — a denial phrase list, then a substring requirement satisfied by its own negation, then a coverage floor met by a different set of records. What it now establishes is that every named release record summarising the adjudication mentions the occurrence it records, which is exactly the defect that occurred: one document corrected and three stale summaries. It cannot establish that such a record says something true, because deciding whether prose is truthful is not something a test does — the original false claim was found by a reader and a deliberate negation would be too. Scoped rather than widened, because an arms race over denial phrasings is one this file had already lost twice.

FOUR OF THE FIVE BLOCKERS IN THE LAST BOUNDED READING WERE IN ORACLES WRITTEN ONE ROUND EARLIER, AND NONE WAS IN THE PACK'S BEHAVIOUR. A sentinel prior carried a placeholder family, so a mutant guarded on a matching family never touched it; the same sentinel was asserted against the ranking function and not against the route that uses it; and the summary guard above was defeated three ways. The subject was correct in every case. Recorded because the readings' findings moved from the release into its tests over four rounds, which is what convergence looks like from the inside and is not the same as being finished.

A READING SCOPED TO A DELTA CANNOT SEE WHAT THE DELTA DID NOT TOUCH, AND THIS RELEASE MISTOOK THAT FOR CONVERGENCE. Three successive bounded readings of three repair deltas found fewer and fewer defects, and the last two found none in the pack's behaviour at all — which was read as the release settling. It was the DELTAS settling. A fourth reading pointed at the modules a consuming project actually calls returned SEVEN reproduced behavioural defects, none of them a test-only finding, in code no repair had touched since the first round. They are closed and pinned in tools/tests/test_behaviour_findings.py. Recorded because the wrong conclusion was drawn from evidence that could not have supported it, and the next release should read the whole subject at least once after its last delta rather than only the delta.

THREE OF THE SEVEN BEHAVIOURAL DEFECTS WERE TWO MECHANISMS ANSWERING ONE QUESTION DIFFERENTLY — the class this release's headline repair was for. `capability_open` called the adapter verifier by a path the repair to `verify_contract` never reached, so readiness reported VERIFIED where the verifier refused; `derive` did not consult a recorded producer where `reconcile` did, so one record was WAITING and RECOVERY_REQUIRED at once; and the projection's headline resolved artifacts against the process while its own panel resolved them against the record, so one page said WAITING and A RESULT IS WAITING TO BE READ. Fixing one caller of a shared question does not fix the question.

EVERY READING OF CODE WRITTEN IN THIS SESSION FOUND DEFECTS IN IT, AND THE RATE DID NOT FALL. A reading of the pack's behaviour found seven; a reading of the repairs for those seven, plus two new tools, found eleven more — ten blocking. Of those eleven, three were the SAME `str(None)` defect the release had fixed in tools/qualification.py hours earlier, remade in a new module; two were repairs that covered some call sites of a shared question and not others; and two were oracles passing for the wrong reason. Newly written code is where this release's defects are, and a reading of it is worth more than another reading of what was already read.

THIS RELEASE SCORED ONE OF ITS OWN MUTATION PASSES INVALIDLY. Six tests fail on ANY byte change because they compare a recorded digest or count; this release labelled them NOT A MUTATION ORACLE so a reader would exclude them, and then ran a mutation pass without excluding them — so every mutant exited non-zero and every verdict read KILLED. Re-scored against a clean baseline, one of the ten had survived. Recorded because the labelling was done for other readers and not applied by the person who wrote it, which is the same shape as a rule stated in prose and not enforced in code.

deferred.RP2.3 DEFER_WITH_TRIGGER: see docs/RP2.3-CAPABILITY-MAP.md for each item and the observation that reopens it: the full routing-evidence schema; the clean-clone reproducibility gate; a commit-subject length ceiling; publication readiness beyond the profile declaration; a write-ceiling runtime for delegation scope.
deferred.RP2.3 REMOVED FROM SCOPE: autonomous termination of a stalled worker (classification ships; ending a worker stays a coordinator action under hitl-matrix row 4), and an observer that restarts a coordinator (DECISIONS.md D23 clause 4).
deferred.RP2.2 DEFER_WITH_TRIGGER: carried unchanged from 2.2.0 — see docs/RP2.2-GATE.md for each item and its trigger.
deferred.EC-O: carried from 2.1.1 — second project blocked by the machine-path rule
deferred.EC-T: carried from 2.1.1 — unscannable-blob volume makes the exemption total unreadable
deferred.EC — a design record's oracle selectors: A design record names a selector per oracle and nothing reads it, so a selector that reaches no test is accepted. The closure matrix already has that mechanism for the release's own oracles; wiring it into the design gate is a new promise rather than a repair. Trigger: the first project whose design records are audited by somebody other than their author.

rejected_for_core.EC-Z: project-specific lesson; would couple Core to one project's internals

evolution_candidates: A DURABLE EVENT LOG. Seven event classes ship because seven are what durable artifacts date; a capability opening, an audit being dispatched and a finding being recorded are not among them, because nothing writes their time down. Trigger: a project wanting a timeline of governance events rather than of artifacts.

A MULTI-YEAR ACTIVITY CALENDAR. Repository activity reads 366 days by default as a render-cost decision, `window_days=0` already reads all of it, and the view names the window it read. Trigger: a project whose history is long enough that the default hides its shape.

RELATIVE YIELD BETWEEN A SAME-FAMILY AND A CROSS-VENDOR AUDIT. The audits are not run as a comparison and a count is not a rate. Trigger: enough paired dispatches on one subject to compare rather than to count.

AN EXECUTION-TRACE ORACLE FOR THE LOOP-ONLY SHAPE, shipped as a tool rather than run once as a measurement. This release traced thirty-six such tests and found none vacuous; nothing stops a thirty-seventh. Trigger: a loop-only test found vacuous, or a project asking for the check.

A READ-ONLY WAY TO ENUMERATE A BUNDLE'S OBJECTS. Establishing that a bundle carries a commit means indexing its pack, which is a write, so a verified bundle whose header names a cited commit yields ANCHOR_UNCONFIRMED and BLOCKS. Trigger: a read-only enumeration becoming available, or a scratch index being authorised.
release_delta: CHANGELOG.md is the canonical per-release delta and tools/release_delta.py checks that this version's entry accounts for what the range added; baseline_revision names the revision it is measured from.
evolution_evidence: policy/recurrence-classes.json is the deduplication mechanism and tools/evolution_evidence.py is its classification and reinforcement path: a recurrence strengthens the class it belongs to with its own provenance, a near-duplicate proposal is returned for a distinction rather than merged or accepted, and occurrences are appended and never collapsed. Engineering-loop failures are classes like any other.
